explanation: Bank line BNK-0025 (2026-08-06, ACH CREDIT ARNOLD LTD, reference INV-1063, +USD 6,595.32) cleared the operating account during the statement period, but a reference search for INV-1063 returns zero ledger entries (bank_transaction_count 1, ledger_entry_count 0), and the case shows reference_matched_elsewhere = false, so the receipt was not recorded under any other reference either. Supporting document DOC-032 is the customer invoice INV-1063 to Arnold Ltd, issue date 2026-06-27, due 2026-07-27, amount due USD 6,595.32 — exactly the amount received, and the timing is consistent with a past-due Net 30 invoice being settled in early August. The invoice is denominated in USD, so no FX conversion is involved, and there is no second bank line or ledger entry for this reference, so it is not a duplicate. This is therefore a genuine customer receipt that cleared the bank but was never booked: a missing ledger entry. Proposed fix: record the cash receipt by debiting 1000 Cash - Operating and crediting 1200 Accounts Receivable for USD 6,595.32 to clear Arnold Ltd's open invoice INV-1063.

Same transaction on both sides: a EUR 7,050.22 vendor payment to Wilkerson-Day for BILL-5060 (vendor bill DOC-021 confirms EUR 7,050.22 due). The foreign amount agrees exactly on both sides; only the USD translation differs. The ledger entry GL-0025 (2026-08-05) used an FX rate of 1.1000, giving USD 7,755.24. The bank actually applied 1.0879, debiting USD 7,669.93 on 2026-08-06 (BNK-0026), which the bank's wire confirmation DOC-004 corroborates (rate 1.0879, USD debited 7,669.93, wire fee USD 0.00 — so no bank-fee component). The 85.31 difference is therefore purely an exchange-rate difference, not a timing, duplicate or fee issue. Because less USD cash left the account than the ledger recorded, cash is understated by 85.31 and the company realised an FX gain. Proposed fix: debit 1000 Cash - Operating 85.31 to bring the cash balance to the actual bank amount of 7,669.93, and credit 7100 FX Gain/Loss 85.31 to record the realised gain. Accounts Payable is untouched, as the full EUR 7,050.22 bill was settled. Note: the one-day date gap (ledger 08-05 vs bank value date 08-06) is a normal settlement lag and does not change the classification.

Same transaction on both sides (reference INV-1021, customer Williams and Sons), recorded in the ledger with the wrong amount. The 2-day date gap (ledger 08-05 vs bank 08-07) is normal ACH settlement lag and does not itself need a correction. Proposed fix: increase cash by USD 900.00 and reduce accounts receivable by the same amount, bringing GL-0017 up to the 7,678.07 actually received and fully clearing the INV-1021 receivable.

Proposed fix: reverse the duplicate entry — debit 1000 Cash - Operating 11,541.85 to restore the cash overstated as paid, and credit 2000 Accounts Payable 11,541.85 to undo the double relief of the vendor liability. Note: the vendor bill is dated 2026-07-17 with Net 30 terms; if the accountant has any record of a genuine second disbursement to James Group clearing after 2026-08-31, this should be re-examined before approval, but nothing in the available data supports that.

Same transaction on both sides, differing only by the exchange rate used. Vendor bill DOC-003 is for EUR 3,812.11 to Ross, Robinson and Bright (due 2026-08-15). Ledger entry GL-0053 (2026-08-11) records the payment of EUR 3,812.11 converted at 1.1000 = USD 4,193.32. The foreign-currency amount is identical on both sides and this is the only appearance of BILL-5058 in the bank and ledger data (no duplicate, no reference matched elsewhere), so this is not an amount-entry error or a timing issue — it is purely an FX rate difference of USD 75.10 (4,268.42 - 4,193.32), an unfavourable FX loss because the actual rate was higher than the booked rate. Proposed fix: debit 7100 FX Gain/Loss USD 75.10 and credit 1000 Cash - Operating USD 75.10, bringing the recorded cash outflow to the USD 4,268.42 the bank actually took. Note for the reviewer: DOC-025 also states a separate USD 35.00 wire fee was debited; that charge is not part of this case's bank line or ledger entry and is not included in this entry — if it appears as its own unreconciled bank line it should be handled under its own case.

Same transaction on both sides: vendor payment to Gray-Mayo for BILL-5059, value date 2026-08-12 on both the bank line (BNK-0055) and the ledger entry (GL-0063), same reference, same foreign amount of GBP 9,400.31. Only the USD amount differs: bank -12,241.08 vs ledger -12,032.40, a difference of 208.68.

The cause is the exchange rate, not the underlying transaction. The bank description and the wire confirmation (DOC-012) both show the bank applied a rate of 1.3022 (GBP 9,400.31 x 1.3022 = USD 12,241.08 debited), while the accountant booked the entry at 1.2800 (GBP 9,400.31 x 1.2800 = USD 12,032.40). The rate gap alone explains the variance exactly: 9,400.31 x (1.3022 - 1.2800) = 208.69, matching the 208.68 difference to a rounding cent.

The vendor bill (DOC-005) confirms the obligation was GBP 9,400.31, so the foreign-currency amount paid was correct and in full - there is no over- or underpayment, no duplicate (only one bank line and one ledger entry carry this reference), and no timing issue (both dated 2026-08-12, within the statement period).

Fix: recognise the unfavourable FX movement. Debit 7100 FX Gain/Loss 208.68 and credit 1000 Cash - Operating 208.68, bringing ledger cash for this payment to the 12,241.08 actually debited by the bank.

One separate note for the reviewer: DOC-012 states a wire fee of USD 35.00 was "debited separately". That fee is not part of this 208.68 difference and is outside the scope of this case; it should be confirmed as either already matched or picked up as its own exception.
